headings: 5.2 NOTIONS OF WORK AND KINETIC ENERGY: THE WORK-ENERGY THEOREM
pages.page_summary: The page derives the work-energy theorem from the kinematic equation for constant acceleration, defining kinetic energy (K) and work (W). It includes Example 5.2, which calculates the work done by gravity and a resistive force on a falling raindrop. Section 5.3 introduces the concept of work for a constant force acting on an object, illustrated by a diagram showing force and displacement vectors.
knowledge_points: The relation v² - u² = 2as is derived from Chapter 3 for rectilinear motion under constant acceleration.
Multiplying the kinematic equation by m/2 yields ½mv² - ½mu² = mas = Fs.
The equation is generalized to three dimensions using vectors: v² - u² = 2a·d.
The vector form of the work-energy relation is ½mv² - ½mu² = m a·d = F·d.
Kinetic energy (K) is defined as 'half the mass times the square of the speed'.
Work (W) is defined as the product of displacement and the component of force along the displacement.
The work-energy theorem states: The change in kinetic energy of a particle is equal to the work done on it by the net force (Kf - Ki = W).
Example 5.2 calculates the work done by gravity (10.0 J) and a resistive force (-8.75 J) on a 1.00 g raindrop falling 1.00 km to a speed of 50.0 m/s.
Work is related to force and the displacement over which it acts.

embedded_text.visual_description: A diagram showing a blue block on a horizontal surface with hatching. A force vector F is shown acting on the block at an angle θ to the horizontal. A displacement vector d is shown along the x-axis.

visuals.description: A schematic diagram illustrating a constant force F acting on an object of mass m. The object is depicted as a blue block on a horizontal surface. The force F is shown as a vector pointing upwards and to the right at an angle θ relative to the horizontal. A displacement d is indicated by a double-headed arrow along the x-axis.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates the geometry of force and displacement vectors for calculating work.
